reference.source: TradingView Help Center, Average Directional Index (ADX)
reference.quote: The Average Directional Index (ADX) is a line that plots in its own pane below the price chart.

draw.today: 29 'adx' labels stamped on the price frame at their signal bars (x 301.5-979, y 67.9-429.6 in the 484px plot), while the concept's own series spec -- ADX with +DI and -DI, fixed 0-100, a level at 25 -- is simultaneously requested and drawn in a bottom pane. ADX therefore draws twice: once correctly below the chart and once as a word at price.
draw.canonical: ADX with +DI and -DI in their own pane below the price, fixed 0-100 with a level at 25; the reference draws the three lines and prints no signal at price, so the 25-cross is read off the pane.

fires.our_rule: ADX(14), +DI(14), -DI(14) are defined on every bar; a label is emitted when ADX crosses 25, or +DI crosses -DI while ADX > 20 (indicator_signals.rs:285-291, n > 30)
fires.their_rule: TradingView plots ADX, +DI and -DI on every bar and marks no cross on the price chart; the cross is a reading of the pane, not a drawn event

rule_as_data.rule: adx = ADX(14); pdi = +DI(14); mdi = -DI(14) => signal when adx[n-1] <= 25 < adx[n], or pdi and mdi cross while adx > 20

warmup.before: ADX needs 14 bars; the detector requires n > 30, so the first possible label is bar 31

reference.quote: The Keltner Channels (KC) indicator is a banded indicator similar to Bollinger Bands and Moving Average Envelopes.

draw.today: 16 'keltner' labels on the price frame (x 185.8-989.7, y 67.9-398.6) while the same concept's three-line Keltner overlay is drawn on the price plot from overlay_series; the word is a second, senseless mark on top of the band it names.
draw.canonical: an EMA(20) centre with upper and lower bands two ATR(10) away, drawn over the candles as a band; the reference calls it 'a banded indicator ... similar to Bollinger Bands' and puts no word at the bar.

fires.our_rule: EMA(20) +/- 2*ATR(10) is defined on every bar; a label is emitted when close is outside the band (indicator_signals.rs:316-318, n > 22)
fires.their_rule: TradingView draws the Keltner band on every bar and marks no breakout at price; the band's edge is itself the signal

rule_as_data.rule: mid = EMA(close, 20); up = mid + 2*ATR(10); lo = mid - 2*ATR(10) => signal when close > up or close < lo

warmup.before: EMA(20) exists from bar 20; the detector requires n > 22

reference.quote: It is a banded indicator consisting of an upper band, lower band and middle line.

draw.today: 0 shapes. The detector never fires -- donchian() includes the current bar in the 20-bar channel (trend.rs:79-95), so close > upper and close < lower are unsatisfiable -- and the three-line overlay that the series route draws is the only Donchian on the chart. The drawing is the reference's channel; the concept's signal does not exist.
draw.canonical: upper, lower and middle lines of the 20-bar channel on the price plot; the reference draws the channel only and marks no breakout, so there is nothing to stamp at the bar.

fires.our_rule: upper/middle/lower are defined on every bar; the breakout clause requires close beyond a channel that already contains that close, so the detector emitted 0 events in 501 bars (indicator_signals.rs:324-326 with trend.rs:79-95)
fires.their_rule: TradingView draws the channel on every bar and marks no breakout; our 0 events match its drawing, but our threshold names a signal the reference never draws

rule_as_data.rule: up = max(high, 20 bars incl. current); lo = min(low, 20 bars incl. current) => signal when close > up or close < lo [unsatisfiable]

warmup.before: the channel exists from bar 20; the detector requires n > 22, and can never fire at any warmup

reference.quote: The calculation of its single line combines trend detection and volatility.

draw.today: 13 'supertrend' labels at signal bars (x 82.9-989.7, y 67.9-416.3) on top of the one-line Supertrend overlay the series route draws. That line is also single-coloured (indicator_series.rs:518-539), so the side the reference encodes in colour is lost, and the label adds a 13th mark at price.
draw.canonical: one trailing line on the price plot, coloured by side -- below price while long, above while short -- because 'its single line combines trend detection and volatility'.

fires.our_rule: the ATR(10)x3 trailing line is defined on every bar; a label is emitted when the line flips side (indicator_signals.rs:336-338, n > 12)
fires.their_rule: TradingView draws the trailing line on every bar and colours it by side; it marks no flip at price

rule_as_data.rule: band = ATR(10) * 3; trend flips when close crosses the trailing stop => signal on side change

warmup.before: ATR(10) exists from bar 10; the detector requires n > 12

reference.quote: The indicator is plotted as dots above or below the price.

draw.today: 38 'psar' labels (x 59.3-1071.1, y 58-454.6) on top of the series route's single pink line. Neither route draws the reference's dots: the overlay is a connected line (indicator_series.rs:541-559), and the only per-bar mark is the word, which says nothing about the stop's value.
draw.canonical: dots above or below the price, one per bar, flipping side with the trend -- 'plotted as dots above or below the price'.

fires.our_rule: SAR(0.02, 0.2) is defined on every bar; a label is emitted when SAR flips above or below price (indicator_signals.rs:346-348, n > 12)
fires.their_rule: TradingView plots every SAR dot and marks no flip separately; the dot's side is the reading

rule_as_data.rule: sar = parabolic_sar(0.02, 0.2) => signal when sar crosses price

warmup.before: SAR exists from bar 2; the detector requires n > 12

reference.quote: The Ichimoku Cloud is a package of multiple technical indicators that signal support, resistance, market trend, and market momentum.

draw.today: 50 'ichimoku' labels (x 661.7-1058.3, y 63-438.1) on top of the series route's tenkan, kijun, chikou lines and kumo fill. Senkou A and B are never stroked (indicator_series.rs:561-595), so the cloud has no edges, and the label adds a 50th mark at price.
draw.canonical: tenkan, kijun and chikou as lines, senkou A/B as the kumo fill and as their own lines, all on the price plot; the cloud is a fill, not a word at the bar.

fires.our_rule: tenkan(9), kijun(26), senkou A/B, chikou(26) are defined on every bar; labels are emitted on tenkan/kijun cross, kijun/price cross, kumo twist and cloud break (indicator_signals.rs:360-380, n > 80)
fires.their_rule: TradingView draws all five lines and the cloud on every bar and marks no cross at price; the cloud's edge is the reference

rule_as_data.rule: tenkan = mid(9); kijun = mid(26); senkou_a = (tenkan+kijun)/2 shifted 26; senkou_b = mid(52) shifted 26 => signals on tenkan/kijun cross, kijun/price cross, kumo twist, close beyond the cloud

warmup.before: senkou B needs 52 + 26 = 78 bars; the detector requires n > 80

reference.quote: The Chandelier Exit, created by Charles Le Beau and popularized by Alexander Elder, is a volatility-based indicator that identifies stop-loss exit points based on local price extremes and Average True Range (ATR).

draw.today: 39 'chandelier' labels (x 67.9-976.8, y 55.3-431.3) on top of two stop lines the series route always draws -- the long stop and the short stop together (indicator_series.rs:736-756), where the canonical chart shows the active one. The label is the third mark at price.
draw.canonical: one active stop line on the price plot: the long stop under the highs while long, the short stop over the lows while short -- never both at once.

fires.our_rule: highest-high(22) - 3*ATR and lowest-low(22) + 3*ATR are defined on every bar; a label is emitted when price crosses the active stop (indicator_signals.rs:77-79, n > 24)
fires.their_rule: TradingView draws the active stop on every bar and marks no exit separately; the line crossing price is the reference

rule_as_data.rule: long_stop = highest(high, 22) - 3*ATR(22); short_stop = lowest(low, 22) + 3*ATR(22) => signal when close crosses the active stop

warmup.before: ATR(22) exists from bar 22; the detector requires n > 24

reference.source: TradingView Help Center, Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) indicator
reference.quote: The indicator plots the MACD and signal values as lines, and the histogram values as color-coded columns.

draw.today: 37 'macd family' labels (x 115-1081.9, y 89.8-409.5) on the price frame while the 23-line family ribbon is drawn in its own pane; the ribbon is the indicator, and the word is a second draw at a scale MACD never uses.
draw.canonical: 23 MACD lines in one pane, zero line, fast-to-slow gradient -- our composition of the reference's MACD pane (line, signal, histogram) repeated across periods, with no mark printed at price.

fires.our_rule: the MACD line for every fast 2..=24 with slow = 2*fast is defined on every bar; a label is emitted when all 23 lines sit on the same side of zero (indicator_signals.rs:554, n > 47)
fires.their_rule: TradingView's MACD pane plots one period continuously and marks no consensus event; there is no external rule for a 23-line ribbon

rule_as_data.rule: for fast in 2..=24: line[fast] = MACD(fast, 2*fast).line => signal when all lines > 0 or all lines < 0

warmup.before: the slowest MACD line exists from bar 52; the consensus detector requires n > 47 and reads whichever lines are defined

reference.source: TradingView community script, Guppy Multiple Moving Average (GMMA)
reference.quote: The GMMA plots two groups of Exponential Moving Averages: short-term and long-term.

draw.today: 11 'ema family' labels (x 162.2-1039, y 94.4-410.7) on the price frame on top of the 12-line GMMA overlay the series route draws; the ribbon is visible, and the word adds a separate mark for the same group cross.
draw.canonical: twelve EMAs on the price plot in two distinguishable groups (3-15 and 30-60) -- 'two groups of Exponential Moving Averages: short-term and long-term' -- with no word at price.

fires.our_rule: 12 EMAs (3..15 and 30..60) are defined on every bar; a label is emitted when the short-group mean crosses the long-group mean (indicator_signals.rs:601-603, n > 62)
fires.their_rule: TradingView draws all twelve GMMA lines continuously and marks no group cross; the compression/expansion of the groups is the reading

rule_as_data.rule: short = mean(EMA(p) for p in 3..=15); long = mean(EMA(p) for p in 30..=60) => signal when short crosses long

warmup.before: EMA(60) exists from bar 60; the detector requires n > 62

reference.source: TradingView Help Center, Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) indicator
reference.quote: The indicator plots the MACD and signal values as lines, and the histogram values as color-coded columns.

draw.today: 50 'macd' labels (x 222.2-1081.9, y 55.3-447.3) at price while the MACD pane -- line, signal, histogram, zero line -- is drawn below the chart. The whole oscillator is already drawn correctly; the labels are 50 copies of its name on the price axis.
draw.canonical: MACD and signal as lines with the histogram as colour-coded columns in their own pane, a zero line -- 'the MACD and signal values as lines, and the histogram values as color-coded columns' -- and no word at price.

fires.our_rule: MACD(12,26,9) line, signal and histogram are defined on every bar; a label is emitted on signal cross or zero cross (indicator_signals.rs:177-184, n > 36)
fires.their_rule: TradingView plots MACD continuously and marks no signal cross; the histogram crossing zero is itself the reading

rule_as_data.rule: line = EMA(12)-EMA(26); signal = EMA(line, 9); hist = line - signal => signal when line crosses signal, or line crosses zero

warmup.before: MACD exists from bar 26; the detector requires n > 36

reference.quote: Exponential Moving Average is very similar to (and is a type of) WMA. The major difference with the EMA is that old data points never leave the average.

draw.today: 3 'ema' labels (x 616.7-751.7, y 63-234.5) while the EMA 20/50/200 overlay is drawn from the series route. Only three 50/200 crosses exist in 501 bars, so the event path is nearly silent while the overlay carries the indicator; the three marks it does make are words at price.
draw.canonical: three EMA lines (20/50/200) on the price plot, price-scaled; a moving average is a continuous line and the reference draws no cross marker.

fires.our_rule: EMA(20), EMA(50) and EMA(200) are defined on every bar; a label is emitted when EMA(50) crosses EMA(200) (indicator_signals.rs:192, n > 201)
fires.their_rule: TradingView plots the EMAs continuously and marks no golden/death cross; the line ordering is the reading

rule_as_data.rule: fast = EMA(close, 50); slow = EMA(close, 200) => signal when fast crosses slow

warmup.before: EMA(200) exists from bar 200; the detector requires n > 201

reference.quote: The Simple Moving Average (SMA) is calculated by adding up the prices of a security over a set period and then dividing that total by the number of periods.

draw.today: 1 'sma' label (x 636, y 179.1) while the SMA 20/50/200 overlay is drawn. A single 50/200 cross in 501 bars makes the event path almost invisible, and the one mark it makes is a word at price.
draw.canonical: three SMA lines (20/50/200) on the price plot, price-scaled; the reference draws the averages as continuous lines and marks no cross.

fires.our_rule: SMA(20), SMA(50) and SMA(200) are defined on every bar; a label is emitted when SMA(50) crosses SMA(200) (indicator_signals.rs:192, n > 201)
fires.their_rule: TradingView plots the SMAs continuously and marks no cross; the line ordering is the reading

rule_as_data.rule: fast = SMA(close, 50); slow = SMA(close, 200) => signal when fast crosses slow

warmup.before: SMA(200) exists from bar 200; the detector requires n > 201
